title: Typing Events
description: Learn how to type React event handlers.

data.text: React events are typed using generics from the React namespace. TypeScript provides specific event types for different DOM elements.

data.title: Event Handlers

data.text: For inline handlers, TypeScript infers the event type from the element.

data.title: Inline Handlers

terms.definition: React's cross-browser wrapper around native events
The element that triggered the event
The element the listener is attached to

data.title: Event Type Inference
data.text: TypeScript automatically infers event types when handlers are attached directly to elements. Explicit types are only needed for separate handler functions.

items.question: Why do event types have generics?
items.answer: The generic parameter specifies the target element type, so TypeScript knows what properties are available on e.target.

items.question: What's the difference between target and currentTarget?
items.answer: target is the element that triggered the event (may be a child element). currentTarget is the element the listener is attached to.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Event type depends on the element
TypeScript infers types for inline handlers
Use explicit types for separate handlers
data.takeaway: Typed events prevent common mistakes in event handling.
